absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt-safety rules for PMU, IBS, branch-record, trace and P4 configuration paths.
State machines and sequencing for enabling, counting, overflow, interrupt delivery and guest or host switching.
MSR numbers, register addresses and hardware access sequences for selection, counter and IBS controls.
Complete sub-event mask enumeration beyond the truncated portion and full counter eligibility constraints.
Implementations behind zero or empty defaults, low-power callback effects, and NMI-safe user copy semantics.

findings.text: IBS op control word places load-latency enable at the top bit and a four bit load-latency threshold ending below it with shift 59. Current count occupies a high field with separate random and extended subfields, while distinct low bits control count mode, valid, enable and L3-miss-only filtering. Maximum count has a 16 bit base form and a wider 23 bit extended form whose upper 7 bits are masked separately.

IBS invalid instruction address is signaled by a mid-word flag at bit 38. A second op control word uses bit 0 as disable, two following bits to exclude samples by privilege address range, and a streaming-store filter bit with shift 3.
In this configuration IBS capability query reports zero and event forwarding reports a missing-entry error, expressing an absent or disabled IBS backend with no other side effects.
Arch perf extended flags reserve one bit for exact attribution and another for guest virtualization context, at bit positions 3 and 5 respectively.
x86 perf register capture pairs a full general register snapshot with a pointer to saved extended vector state, allowing variable length media register data alongside fixed CPU state.
Arch misc-flag accessors are defined as self-named hooks for host and guest contexts, so this header adds no selection logic and defers to an arch supplied implementation of the same name.

Caller-register capture fills only instruction pointer from the supplied address, stack pointer from the current frame, code segment from the kernel code selector, and clears flags; remaining register content is not preserved by this operation.
Guest switch descriptor carries one MSR identifier plus two 64 bit values representing host and guest contents, supporting save and restore across virtualization transitions.
Branch-record descriptor records entry count and index bounds for from, to and info arrays plus a boolean indicating whether call-stack reconstruction is available.
Default PMU helpers clear the capability structure, report zero hardware event configuration, and provide empty local-APIC and microcode hooks, indicating no platform setup in this configuration.
Default branch-record query clears the caller supplied descriptor. The virtualization notification for processor trace accepts an on or off indication but performs no action here.
Low-power perf callback support is marked required, and the inline entry forwards its boolean low-power state to a static-call target.
AMD PMU virtualization enable and disable helpers are empty in this header. Arch perf output copy is aliased to the NMI-safe user copy helper.
Pentium 4 perf header uses a single include-once marker to prevent repeated inclusion.

NetBurst perf topology defines 46 event selection registers with 2 reserved, leaving 44 usable, and 18 counters. Counter values are 40 bits wide with an all-ones mask and a boundary bit at position 39 used to distinguish flagged state.

Event selection register layout separates event number, sub-event mask and tag fields at distinct offsets, plus a tag-enable bit and four privilege bits selecting operating system and user counting for each of two hardware threads. Constructors shift plain event, mask and tag values into their field positions.

Counter control layout provides overflow, cascade and forced-overflow flags, per-thread overflow interrupt routing, edge detection, a four bit threshold at shift 20, complement and compare modifiers, an ESCR selector field, an enable bit, single, both and any thread modes, and a reserved low field. Helpers shift threshold and selector values into place.

A 64 bit event configuration stores the selection value in the upper half and counter control in the lower half, with extractors for each half and for event-number and sub-event subfields. The top bit records hardware-thread identity and bit 9 marks aliasable configurations.

Configuration masks distinguish comparable event identity from per-instance state: selection mask covers event, sub-event and tag controls, counter mask covers edge, threshold and comparison controls plus thread and reserved bits, and alias comparison uses a narrower counter subset. Thread identity, privilege, overflow, cascade, interrupt routing and aliasable marker are treated as immutable non-alias state.

Helpers test cascade mode, read and set or clear thread identity, detect active multithreading and current logical thread, decide whether thread-specific state must swap by comparing configured and current threads, and build default counter and selection values with any-thread counting, per-thread interrupt routing and requested privilege inclusion.

Default counter and selection values depend on detected sibling-thread identity, so callers must re-evaluate after CPU migration and honor the thread-swap decision or counts and overflow interrupts may be attributed to the wrong logical processor.

NetBurst event families form an enumerated set spanning trace cache, branch prediction, memory, bus, execution and retirement behavior. Each opcode packs an event identifier in the high byte and a selection index in the low byte with accessors for each part, and the opcode table binds every family to its hardware code and documents eligible selection register and counter pairings.

Sub-event mask enumerators are generated by shifting a single-bit position into the selection mask field under a family and subcase naming scheme. The visible prefix covers trace delivery, fetch, TLB, memory, replay, page walk, queue, cache, bus and allocation families with their documented subcases.
